verification.note: Confirmed by reading the code. In CompleteStep.test.tsx:74-77 the test waits only until mockFetch has been called. CompleteStep.tsx:33-38 calls fetch synchronously in the click handler when onBeforeSubmit is undefined, so the waitFor callback passes on its first check. The test does not wait for `await fetch`, the `!res.ok` branch, `await res.json()` (:49), setError (:54) or the finally block (:61-63) to run. The negative assertion at :77 therefore makes no explicit guarantee about the failure branch. A regression that called loadFullPage after the json await, for example, could run after the assertion and the test would not detect it. I did not run the tests. Whether RTL's asyncWrapper/act happens to flush enough microtasks is not established by the test itself.

unspecified_scores.reason: After a successful unlock (unlock/page.tsx:42-44) or complete-setup (CompleteStep.tsx:61-63), the button becomes clickable again during the short window before the browser navigates; on a home LAN the user would rarely see or click it, and a second click at most sends a redundant request or flashes an error before the page load.

specification_compliance: The success path of CompleteStep calls loadFullPage('/admin') (CompleteStep.tsx:58), and the success test asserts this (CompleteStep.test.tsx:57-59).
regression_risks: The CompleteStep failure test would not reliably detect a regression that calls loadFullPage late in the failure branch, because it does not await the error state.
test_coverage: CompleteStep failure test: the negative assertion runs before the failure branch has settled. Awaiting the error text (for example, findByText of the error message) would make it meaningful.
not_verified: Did not run vitest, so the actual microtask ordering under RTL's waitFor/act wrapper is not checked empirically.
